meta.scalability_note: 4 EU regions (Frankfurt, Berlin, Karlsruhe, Nuremberg); basic auto-scaling for VMs and Kubernetes; no serverless compute; no global CDN; horizontal scaling limited compared to hyperscalers
meta.performance_note: 99.9% SLA for compute services; ISO 27001 certified German data centers; low-latency EU backbone; GDPR-compliant infrastructure by design

AWS Amplify.note: No managed web or mobile app hosting platform. Applications must be deployed on VMs or Kubernetes.

AWS Lambda.note: No FaaS or serverless function service available. Workloads requiring event-driven compute must use VMs or Kubernetes Jobs.

Amazon ECS.note: No managed container orchestration service equivalent to ECS. Container workloads are deployed via Managed Kubernetes only.

Amazon EKS.note: Fully managed Kubernetes service with auto-scaling, multi-AZ support, and automated upgrades across EU regions.

Amazon EC2.note: Broad VM portfolio including Flex, Cube, and GPU instances. Available across all EU regions with on-demand and reserved pricing.

AWS Batch.note: No managed batch job processing service. Batch workloads require manual orchestration via VMs or Kubernetes Jobs.

AWS Elastic Beanstalk.note: No PaaS application deployment platform. Deployments are managed manually via VMs or Kubernetes.

Amazon S3.note: S3-compatible object storage available across EU regions. Supports standard S3 API, versioning, and access policies.

Amazon S3 Glacier.note: No dedicated archive or cold storage tier. Long-term data retention requires standard object storage or self-managed solutions.

Amazon EBS.note: SSD-backed persistent block volumes, attachable to Compute Engine instances. Supports snapshots and resizing.

AWS Backup.note: VM and volume snapshots are available but there is no centralised cross-service backup policy management equivalent to AWS Backup.

Amazon EFS.note: No managed elastic NFS-compatible shared file system. Shared storage requires self-hosted NFS or third-party solutions.

Amazon RDS.note: Fully managed PostgreSQL and MySQL with automated backups, point-in-time recovery, and high-availability failover.

Amazon DocumentDB.note: No managed MongoDB-compatible document database service. Self-hosting required.

Amazon DynamoDB.note: No managed NoSQL key-value or document database. Self-hosted alternatives such as Cassandra or DynamoDB-compatible APIs must be deployed on VMs.

Amazon Timestream.note: No managed time-series database service. Self-hosted InfluxDB or TimescaleDB required.

Amazon Aurora.note: No managed high-performance relational database engine. IONOS Managed Database covers standard PostgreSQL and MySQL only.

Amazon ElastiCache.note: No managed in-memory caching service. Redis or Memcached must be self-hosted on VMs or Kubernetes.

Amazon Redshift.note: No managed cloud data warehouse service. Analytical workloads require self-hosted solutions such as ClickHouse or Redshift-compatible engines.

AWS Application Load Balancer.note: Managed HTTP/HTTPS load balancer with path-based and host-based routing, SSL termination, and health checks.

AWS Network Load Balancer.note: TCP load balancing is supported. Advanced UDP routing and cross-zone features are limited compared to AWS NLB.

Amazon VPC.note: Full private networking environment with subnets, routing tables, firewall rules, and VPN gateway support.

Amazon Route 53.note: Managed DNS service with support for all standard record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, etc.).

Amazon API Gateway.note: No managed API gateway service. API management requires self-hosted solutions such as Kong or nginx.

Amazon CloudFront.note: No global CDN service available. Content delivery requires third-party CDN providers.

AWS Direct Connect.note: No dedicated private connectivity service equivalent to Direct Connect. Private peering arrangements are handled on a case-by-case basis.

Amazon Rekognition.note: No managed computer vision or image/video analysis service. Self-hosted or third-party AI APIs required.

Amazon SageMaker.note: No managed ML platform for training or inference. Workloads must be deployed on GPU VMs or Kubernetes with self-managed ML frameworks.

Amazon Bedrock.note: No managed generative AI or foundation model API service. Self-hosted LLM deployments on GPU instances are required.

AWS Glue.note: No managed ETL or data integration service. Data pipelines must be self-hosted using Apache Spark or similar frameworks.

Amazon EMR.note: No managed big data processing cluster service. Hadoop or Spark clusters must be self-deployed on VMs.

Amazon Athena.note: No serverless interactive query service for object storage. Self-hosted Trino or Presto required.

AWS IAM.note: Role-based access control with users, groups, roles, and resource-level policies. Supports API tokens and fine-grained permissions.

Amazon Cognito.note: No managed identity and user pool service for applications. Self-hosted Keycloak or Auth0 integration required.

AWS IAM Identity Center.note: No SSO or centralized identity federation service. Federated access must be configured manually.

AWS KMS.note: No managed key management service. Encryption key management requires third-party HSM integration or self-managed solutions.

AWS Secrets Manager.note: No managed secrets storage or rotation service. HashiCorp Vault or similar must be self-hosted.

AWS Certificate Manager.note: TLS certificates can be provisioned and attached via the load balancer integration; no standalone managed PKI or automated certificate lifecycle service.

Amazon GuardDuty.note: No managed threat detection or intelligent security monitoring service. External SIEM solutions must be integrated.

AWS Security Hub.note: No unified security posture management dashboard. Security findings must be aggregated externally.

AWS Config.note: No managed resource configuration compliance and audit service. Configuration management requires external tooling.

AWS Shield.note: Basic network-level DDoS mitigation is included in the platform. No advanced application-layer DDoS protection equivalent to AWS Shield Advanced.

AWS WAF.note: No managed web application firewall service. WAF functionality requires self-hosted solutions such as ModSecurity.

AWS CloudTrail.note: Basic API audit logs are available in the management console. Limited log export options and retention configuration compared to CloudTrail.

Amazon CloudWatch.note: Basic VM and infrastructure metrics with alerting. Less integrated and with fewer data sources than CloudWatch. No log aggregation equivalent.

Amazon SNS.note: No managed pub/sub notification service. Webhook-based alerts from monitoring are available but no full SNS equivalent.

AWS Systems Manager.note: No managed operations management platform for patching, inventory, or remote session management.

AWS Cost Explorer.note: Detailed billing dashboard with resource-level cost breakdown, usage history, and invoice management.

AWS CodeBuild.note: No managed CI build service. CI/CD pipelines must use self-hosted or third-party tools such as GitLab CI or Jenkins.

AWS CodeDeploy.note: No managed application deployment automation service.

AWS CodePipeline.note: No managed CI/CD pipeline orchestration service.

Amazon ECR.note: Managed Docker/OCI-compatible container image registry. Supports private repositories and Kubernetes integration.

AWS CloudFormation.note: No native IaC templating service. Official IONOS Terraform provider is available for infrastructure automation.

AWS IoT Core.note: No managed IoT connectivity or device gateway service. IoT broker must be self-hosted (e.g., Eclipse Mosquitto).

AWS IoT Device Management.note: No managed IoT device fleet management or over-the-air update service.

Amazon SQS.note: No managed message queue service. RabbitMQ or Apache Kafka must be self-hosted on VMs or Kubernetes.

Amazon EventBridge.note: No managed event bus or serverless event routing service.

AWS Step Functions.note: No managed serverless workflow orchestration service. Workflow automation requires self-hosted solutions such as Apache Airflow.

Amazon SES.note: No managed transactional email sending service. Third-party SMTP providers or self-hosted Postfix required.

Amazon Kinesis.note: No managed real-time data streaming service. Self-hosted Apache Kafka or Redpanda required.
